We have a target molecule: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to propose route using templates.

We have found template 733 which seems to be a sulfonamide formation from aryl sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-aryl) and an aniline (Ar-NH2). The retro reaction: product is sulfonamide; reactants are aryl sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

The template's retro_smarts: [O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]

Thus disconnection: target sulfonamide can be broken into aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl) and aniline (Ar-NH2). In our target, the sulfonamide is between two aryl groups: left side is p-tolyl (CH3-Ph) with sulfonamide attached to para position; right side is phenyl with a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (i.e., trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the right aryl (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the right aryl ring (the one bearing the side chain). The left aryl is attached to the nitrogen as part of the sulfonamide? Wait: SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Interpretation: tolyl ring (c1) with substituent NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the nitrogen attached to tolyl is the sulfonamide nitrogen (Ar-NH-SO2-Ar'). So left side is tolyl (Ar-NH-). Right side is aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor (Ar'-SO2-Cl). So we can disconnect to tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (the right aryl with side chain). So step 1: sulfonamide formation.

Now we need to get the right aryl sulfonyl chloride. The right aryl is phenyl with side chain: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So we need to make aryl sulfonyl chloride from that aryl. Typically sulfonyl chloride can be made from sulfonic acid (SO3H) or from sulfonylation of aryl with chlorosulfonic acid. But we can consider a retrosynthetic step: aryl sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the corresponding aryl sulfonic acid (Ar-SO3H) via chlorination, or from the aryl via sulfonation of benzene? However we need commercially available leaves. Perhaps the aryl sulfonyl chloride is commercially available? Let's check if such compound is available: 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride? The aryl is 4-(E-... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride. Might not be commercially available.

Alternative: we could disconnect the amide side chain: the right aryl has an amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). That is an anilide (aryl amide). Could break that amide via retrosynthesis: amide formation from carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline. So we could have step 2: amide formation between a cinnamic acid derivative (or acryloyl) and an aniline (p-aminophenyl). The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Actually /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N: that's trans-α,β-unsaturated carbonyl attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the amide is between cinnamic acid (or trans-cinnamoyl) and p-aminophenyl. So we can disconnect amide: get trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-cinnamoyl chloride) and p-aminophenyl (aniline with NH2). The trans-cinnamic acid is commercially available.

Thus route: Step 1: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (commercial) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (which we need to get). Step 2: aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonylation of the aryl (the right aryl) with chlorosulfonic acid? But we could also consider making sulfonyl chloride from the corresponding sulfonic acid, which could be made via sulfonation of the aryl (electrophilic aromatic substitution) using SO3 or fuming sulfuric acid, then chlorination. However that may be more steps.

Alternative: maybe we can reverse order: first make the amide, then sulfonylate the resulting aniline? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the left tolyl, not the right. So the right aryl is sulfonyl chloride; the left is aniline. So we need the right aryl sulfonyl chloride. Could we instead make the sulfonyl chloride from the right aryl after amide formation? The right aryl after amide formation is still the same aryl (phenyl with side chain). So we could first form the amide (step 1) to get the right aryl amide (i.e., 4-(E-... )-phenyl-sulfonyl? Actually the amide is attached to the right aryl via the side chain, not to the sulfonyl group. The sulfonyl group is attached directly to the aryl ring (para position). So the amide side chain is attached to the aryl ring at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the aryl ring has two substituents: sulfonyl (SO2-) attached to left side (connected to nitrogen) and the side chain (cinnamoyl anilide) attached at para position. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor would have the side chain already present (the amide). So we could first make the amide (step 1) on that aryl, then sulfonyl chloride formation (step 2), then sulfonamide formation (step 3). That's 3 steps.

Thus leaves: p-toluidine (commercial), trans-cinnamic acid (commercial), p-aminophenyl (aniline) (commercial), chlorosulfonic acid (maybe not commercial? but could be). However we need leaves to be commercially available chemicals. Chlorosulfonic acid is a reagent, likely commercially available. Also we may need thionyl chloride for converting sulfonic acid to sulfonyl chloride. But we can treat sulfonyl chloride formation as a single step using chlorosulfonic acid on the aryl (direct sulfonyl chloride). That reagent is commercial.

Thus propose route:

Target (T) = p-tolyl-sulfonamide-aryl.

Step 3 (final): Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride -> target. Template 733.

Step 2: Synthesize aryl sulfonyl chloride (R-Ph-SO2Cl) from aryl sulfonic acid (R-Ph-SO3H) using chlorination (e.g., SOCl2). But we can use template for sulfonyl chloride formation? Not needed; we can just state that chlorination of sulfonic acid yields sulfonyl chloride. Leaves: aryl sulfonic acid (which can be made from sulfonation of aryl). However we need to keep steps <=3, so we need to get aryl sulfonyl chloride directly from aryl via chlorosulfonic acid (direct sulfonyl chloride). That is a single step (electrophilic aromatic substitution). So step 2: electrophilic aromatic sulfonyl chloride formation: aryl (with side chain) + chlorosulfonic acid -> aryl sulfonyl chloride. Template? Might not have a template but we can just propose.

Step 1: Amide formation: trans-cinnamic acid + p-aminophenyl -> aryl side chain amide (the side chain attached to aryl). Use amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Template for amide formation? Could use a template that forms amide from acid chloride and amine. But we can propose using standard coupling.

Thus leaves: p-toluidine, trans-cinnamic acid, p-aminophenyl (4-aminophenyl), chlorosulfonic acid.

Check commercial availability and price sum < $9999. Likely yes.

Now we need to produce JSON route with up to 3 steps. The format: root molecule with children reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 733 for sulfonamide formation. Need template for amide formation (maybe template ID for amide formation). Let's search for amide formation (functional_groups_formed: amide).
